The Allied Peoples Movement and the All Progressives Congress have disagreed over the Federal Government’s spending priorities, with the APM accusing President Bola Tinubu’s administration of neglecting Nigerians amid economic hardship and insecurity. The party alleged that while millions of citizens struggle with hunger, poverty, and poor access to basic services, political officeholders continue to enjoy lavish privileges at public expense. Speaking at a stakeholders’ meeting with party members in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday, the South-West Coordinator of the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Eddy Olafeso, accused Tinubu of abandoning “the welfare of ordinary Nigerians.” Olafeso, a former National Vice Chairman (South-West) of the Peoples Democratic Party, described the APC’s years in power as a period of denial, destruction, and hunger. He faulted the Federal Government’s spending priorities following the removal of the petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, citing the acquisition of a presidential jet, a yacht, and luxury vehicles for political appointees. Olafeso expressed concern that while Nigerians struggle to access affordable healthcare and other essential services, the government continues to spend heavily on the comfort of political officeholders. They are coming back to continue to have this opportunity to rape our country,” he said. The former PDP chieftain also listed unemployment, displacement, homelessness, out-of-school children, kidnapping, and killings among the challenges confronting Nigerians. He questioned the Federal Government’s handling of major infrastructure projects—particularly the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Badagry-Sokoto road—and called for greater transparency in the country’s crude oil production costs and revenue. Olafeso, however, expressed confidence in the ability of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, to address the country’s challenges, describing him as a credible alternative capable of restoring prosperity. Stable power supply key to achieving $1tn economy – Minister Ogun seeks stronger emergency response to curb preventable deaths 2027: BOOT gov candidate promises stable power supply in Ogun “I have no doubt whatsoever that Seyi Makinde, our candidate, can reset Nigeria and bring back the good times we are all looking for: very good schools, very good health facilities across the country, and infrastructure all over the country,” he said. Responding, the APC Director of Publicity, Bala Ibrahim, dismissed the criticism, saying the ruling party has the membership and support base to account for its campaign spending. He stated that the relevant question is whether the party’s expenditure exceeds the limits approved by the Independent National Electoral Commission. Ibrahim said, “The capacity, strength, support base, and membership strength of the APC cannot be equated with those of the APM or API or whatever their name is. The APC is in control of 36 states plus Abuja, while they are in control of just one state or a few local governments. “So, if the party has the capacity, membership, and support base of people who can contribute to its campaign, what is wrong with that? The question to ask is whether the money being spent is outside or beyond the amount approved by INEC for political parties. I can bet you that the APC is not doing that. As a progressive and law-iding party, the APC will not exceed the amount approved for it.” Earlier, the Ogun State chairman of the APM, Abayomi Sanyaolu, described Makinde’s candidacy as a new direction in the country’s political conversation. Sanyaolu pledged the commitment of party leaders to building a strong and united political structure capable of mobilising support across local government areas, wards, and polling units in Ogun State. He stated that Nigeria needs economic recovery, functional institutions, and governance that prioritises citizens’ welfare. Also speaking, the APM governorship candidate in Ogun State, Rotimi Babajide, called for improved governance, infrastructure, and public services, saying residents deserve leadership that prioritises their welfare. Babajide pledged that the party will actively mobilise support for Makinde’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Olufemi Adediran
